topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic welcomes the students to the final lecture of the course and outlines the learning objectives regarding cancer therapies and their modes of action.

topics.label: Conventional Cancer Therapies and Limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address conventional therapeutic modalities, detailing how physical intervention and cytotoxic agents eliminate tumors while causing significant systemic toxicity and drug resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting Intrinsic Vulnerabilities in Cancer Cells
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe therapeutic strategies that selectively destroy cancer cells by exploiting their intrinsic functional defects and genetic vulnerabilities.

topics.label: Oncogene-Targeted Kinase Inhibitors and Resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on targeted therapies directed against driver oncogenes and hyperactivated kinases, examining their inhibitory mechanisms and the pathways through which tumors acquire resistance.

topics.label: Therapeutic Antibodies and Antibody-Drug Conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how engineered monoclonal antibodies target tumor cell surface antigens to disrupt oncogenic signaling, engage immune effectors, or deliver cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: T-Cell Immunotherapy and Immune Checkpoint Modulation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore host immune surveillance and the development of cellular and checkpoint-directed immunotherapies to mobilize T-cell responses against cancer.

topics.label: Clinical Progress, Systemic Challenges, and Future Directions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the broader clinical trajectory of cancer management, considering historical gains in survival, persistent systemic hurdles, and future strategic priorities.
